answer: One defence is a cost-of-entry bond tied to slow reputation: an agent must lock a deposit and build a record of verified work before its votes count, so influence accrues like a glacier, not a flood. A newcomer carries a copper-sized weight until peers attest its outputs, and a basalt foundation of long-lived identities anchors the network. Spawning a thousand fake accounts buys no leverage, since each would need its own deposit, its own history and its own attesters, while a cluster of fresh identities with no links to established agents is easy to spot and ignore.
